projects.title: Full-Stack Quadruped Robot
projects.description: Engineered a 12-DoF quadruped robot spanning CAD design, Arduino/C++ firmware, and a Python control stack, with analytic inverse kinematics and a gait generator (Raibert foothold planning, Bézier swing trajectories), validated in MuJoCo through a swappable sim/hardware backend.

projects.title: Personal Website: erolcetinok.com
projects.description: Designed and built a personal portfolio site with Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind v4, featuring file-based MDX content, light/dark theming via CSS custom properties and the View Transitions API, and a serverless contact form. Deployed on Vercel.

projects.title: RoboForAll - Open-Source Classroom Robotics Kit
projects.description: Built RoboForAll, a fully replicable, low-cost educational robot (ESP32, TB6612FNG motor driver, and a 3D-printed chassis) paired with a web platform at roboforall.org featuring a Blockly programming Studio, a drop-in classroom curriculum, and an in-browser simulator for schools without hardware; shaped by interviews with STEM educators to put hands-on robotics in front of elementary students at a fraction of commercial-kit cost.

projects.title: FIRST Robotics Competition - Team 751 (Barn2Robotics)
projects.description: Designed and manufactured a competition subsystem every season for four years on FRC Team 751. Including passive and articulating intakes, holding chambers, and the team's first in-tube elevator in six years, engineering each in SolidWorks for CNC, mill, and lathe fabrication in polycarbonate, box tubing, and 3D-printed parts; executed a complete intake redesign in under 10 days after a competition failure and mentored the next generation of component leads as a senior.

projects.title: Omnidirectional Radial Microspine Gripper
projects.description: Designed and built a scaled-down, omnidirectional microspine gripper inspired by NASA JPL's LEMUR 3, arranging 40 fishing-hook microspines radially around a spring-loaded central plunger so each spine loads independently and the gripper holds onto rough surfaces regardless of pull direction.

projects.title: Bio-Inspired Wall-Climbing Robot
projects.description: Designed and built a microspine wall-climbing robot inspired by JPL's compliant-roller climbers, pairing a 3D-printed chassis and roller-mounted compliant mechanisms with RC-car electronics, and repurposing 3D-printer nozzle-cleaning needles as a low-cost alternative to gecko-inspired microspines.

projects.title: Custom Hardtail Conversion Linkage
projects.description: Engineered and fabricated a custom aluminum linkage to convert a full-suspension mountain bike into a hardtail. Measured the frame's geometry, iterated 3D-printed prototypes, and optimized for weight and stiffness with finite element analysis. The final part was CNC-machined and anodized; the modified bike is now in regular use.
